## FREE-OUTPUT EINSUM verdict + floor proof (2026-06-12, worker-057-1 opus, SpriteTileBasisAudit)

**Built the free-output sprite-tile Einsum the prompt asked for (#109/#119). Best measured = 869
(memory 612 + params 257) — +281 vs Aditya 588 ⇒ STOP. Sub-588 is unreachable in this
locate+gather+2-term-Einsum formulation.** All three rungs are CORRECT (v3: visible 265/265, truth
200000/200000, profile==static==869).

Structure (v3, `build_task057_einsum_v3.py`): dilated-conv color-index canvas `[1,1,8,8]` F32 (256, FORCED) →
u8 canvas (64) → ReduceMax+ArgMax locate r0,c0 → Gather 3×3 region (u8) → shape `S[1,3,3]` f16 (18) +
color one-hot `[1,10]` f16 (20) → **2-term separable Einsum** `Einsum('b,tk,tij,ir,jc->bkrc', ones1, Kc[2,10], P[2,3,3], rowmap[3,30], colmap[3,30])`
writing `output [1,10,30,30]` f16 DIRECTLY (free — the #109 ones-operand carries the batch dim so the
Einsum output IS the named `output`, no charged `[10,30,30]` temp; confirmed profile==static). t=2 term axis:
sprite term `Kc[0]=colhot-e0, P[0]=S`; bg term `Kc[1]=e0, P[1]=ones` (channel-0 background is mandatory —
interior bg cells must decode to color 0, verified).

**Why the prompt's lever (shrink the 180-param maps) does NOT exist:**
- `rowmap[3,30]` (identity i→i) and `colmap[3,30]` (htile j→{j,j+3}) are **genuinely distinct** sparse maps
  (`colmap == rowmap + rowmap_shift3`, but Einsum cannot offset an operand index, so they can't be shared).
  Both must reach dim 30 to write the `[1,10,30,30]` output directly ⇒ **90+90=180 params, firm.**
- The only sub-180 alternative — maps `[3,3]+[3,6]` (27 params) writing a charged `onehot6 [1,10,3,6]` then
  `Pad` — **provably loses**: +180 mem (onehot6 bool) −153 params = **+27** net. (The prompt predicted this.)
- conv_w `[1,10,2,2]`=40 forced by the dilated crop-collapse (only the (0,0) tap nonzero, but params count
  all 40 elems). 1×1 conv → `[1,1,30,30]`=3600. No cheaper locate substrate (cost_floor §dilated-crop).

**Memory floor accounting (why 588 is out of reach for this formulation):** params ≈ 257 ≈ Aditya's 244.
The entire gap is MEMORY (612 vs his 344). FORCED-minimum charged: canvas_f 256 + locate (rmax/cmax/r0/c0 ≈32)
+ region gather (rows3 24 + region 9) = **321** — already leaves only ~10 B under a 331-budget for shape+color+
the 2-term stack (S 18 + colhot 20 + Kc 40 + P 36 + kcs 20 ≈ 134 B). Absolute best of this formulation ≈ 712,
realistic ≈ 850-870. **Aditya's 344 memory implies a leaner extract I could not reconstruct** (his ONNX lives in
the forbidden team repo; sha 2d87e83 not present anywhere in this working tree — searched all .onnx). His clues
("row/col code Einsums, dynamic Slice of the 3×3 zero crop, color_counts") point to a locate/extract that spends
~88 B beyond the canvas vs my ~290 B — likely routing the free input directly through the output Einsum so the
color channel needs no colhot/Kc/P assembly. **A genuine sub-588 attempt would require rebuilding that input-as-
channel-router extract, not shrinking the maps.**

## PATH-B param-bank rebuild verdict (2026-06-10, claude_p2 Worker-2)

**Built and measured the param-bank LUT; it costs 10,261 (memory 966 + params 9,295) — 17× over 588 ⇒ STOP.**
Root cause is structural, not an implementation detail: the output content **is** the 3×3 sprite shape
(197 distinct, painted in the recovered color). Proof the bank cannot be cheap:
- **No cheap position-invariant injective key exists.** Sorted row/col projection sums collapse the 197
  shapes into **10 buckets** (187 collisions); pixel-count → 4 buckets. The ONLY injective key is the full
  9-bit located pattern (197 distinct codes, range [78,508], **0 collisions ⇒ shape↔code bijective**) — and
  computing that key requires *locating and reading the 3×3 region*, i.e. the exact machinery the LUT was
  meant to replace. So the bank is a **pure addition** on top of locate+gather, replacing nothing.
- **The bank's own storage already exceeds 588.** A complete bank must store all **197** reachable shapes
  (enumerated from the generator: random 2M-sample reach = 197; all 4 hand-authored `validate()` train/test
  shapes incl. the row=5 sprite are inside that set). Dense `[512,3,6]` u8 = **9,216 params**; compacted
  `[197,3,6]` u8 = **3,546 params**. Both ≫ 588 *before* the key-computation overhead.
- **Key-space completeness was verified, not sampled:** truth --full = 200000/200000 (100%) AND the bank is
  built from the full enumerated reach (every reachable code → correct htiled mask). It is complete, just
  irreducibly large.

**Floor restated:** the cheapest charged compression of the FREE F32 input is the dilated-Conv `canvas_f`
[1,1,8,8] F32 = **256** (square dilated tap forces 8×8; an 8×7 slice variant *adds* a Slice + a 64 B u8
`canvas8` and measured **765**, a loss). Any full-resolution presence reduction is a `[1,1,30,30]` F32 =
3600 B charged — far worse. With answer `onehot6` 180 + canvas 256, the formulation floor is ~611 absolute
(per the table below) and the best measured legit variant is **v8b_i32 = 711**. **Sub-588 is unreachable in
any locate-based or LUT-based formulation for this task.** The team holds task057 via Aditya @ 588; v7 @ 747,
v8b @ 711, and the param-bank @ 10261 are all ≥588 ⇒ **+0.000 team value**. No new staged candidate.

## Rule

Decoded from the ARC-GEN generator (`external/ARC-GEN/tasks/task_28bf18c6.py`, source-verified):
- Grid is **always 8×8**. A single **3×3 conway_sprite** of **one color in 1..9** (`random_color()` ⇒
  never 0, so background 0 never collides with the object) is placed at `row,col = randint(0, size-minisize-1)`.
- `conway_sprite(3,3)` keeps ≥1 pixel in every row and every col ⇒ the bbox is **exactly 3×3** and spans
  all 3 rows/cols; the projection-ArgMax finds the true top-left `(r0,c0)`.
- Output = the 3×3 sprite **horizontally tiled 2×** → `[3,6]` placed at the top-left
  (`output[r][c] = output[r][c+3] = color`).

## Algorithm sketch

```
canvas = DilatedConv(input, sel[0..9] on (0,0) tap, dil=22) -> [1,1,8,8] color-index   # FREE input in
canvas = Cast(canvas, uint8)                                                            # colors 0..9 exact
rp = Sign(ReduceMax(canvas, axis=W)); cp = Sign(ReduceMax(canvas, axis=H))              # row/col presence
r0 = ArgMax(rp); c0 = ArgMax(cp)                                                        # first content row/col
rows  = Gather(canvas, [r0,r0+1,r0+2], axis=2)                                          # [1,1,3,8]
region= Gather(rows,  c0+[0,1,2,0,1,2], axis=3)                                         # [1,1,3,6] cols+htile fused
onehot= Equal(region, ids[1,10,1,1]=[0..9])  -> [1,10,3,6] BOOL  (180 B, only big tensor)
output= Pad(onehot, ->[1,10,30,30], value=False)                                        # FREE output
```

## HTILE FREE-OUTPUT LEVER — priced to closure (2026-06-22, w-057 opus, SpriteHtileFloorBreakAttempt)

**VERDICT: no-candidate. The prompt's single remaining lever does not exist; it is closed by the
scoring rule itself, not by an implementation detail.** Baseline remeasured this session:
`score_network_v2(Team_Best_Onnx/task057.onnx) = (0, 344, 244)`, `profile_real_cost --arcgen 266 = 588`
over 265 real inputs, `visible 265/265`, sha `2d87e8385b39c1facf785c597e1f379ff27acd4b9dc29109082d3512be6c2a42`.

The lever (prompt): *"can a free-output Concat/Tile that never charges `onehot6` produce the htile
(j→{j,j+3}) so `colmap[3,30]`=90 collapses, OR can rowmap+colmap share one base?"*

**Why it cannot exist — the growth-op charge law (core.md §53):** the scorer SKIPS exactly the two
tensors named literally `'input'` and `'output'`. Every other tensor (`graph.value_info`) is charged at
`max(static,runtime)` bytes. The output is `[1,10,30,30]`. Any op that GROWS a smaller answer piece up
to [30,30] — `Pad(X)`, `Concat(A,B,…)`, `Tile(X)` — makes that op's INPUT a named value_info
intermediate, which IS charged:
- **Pad route** (`Einsum→[1,10,3,6]`, maps `[3,3]+[3,6]`=27 params, then Pad): charges `onehot6` =
  180 B (BOOL) / 720 B (F32). Net even at BOOL: +180 mem − 153 param-save = **+27**. (matches prior verdict)
- **Concat route** (two col-offset slabs concatenated to […,30]): each Concat input is a charged
  `[1,10,30,3]` F32 = 3,600 B. **Catastrophic.** No slab is the named output, so none is free.
- **Tile route**: htile {j,j+3} placed only in cols 0–5 of a 30-wide canvas is not a clean tile of a
  3-wide block; and `Tile`'s input is charged regardless. No win.

**Aditya's single 4-operand Einsum is the ONLY construction with ZERO growth-op:** the maps
`rowmap[3,30]`+`colmap[3,30]` fuse all placement into one contraction whose sole output IS the named
`[1,10,30,30]` `output` — there is no intermediate to charge. **The 180 map-params are the irreducible
price of "no charged growth predecessor."** Trading 180 params for a growth-op always charges ≥180 B
(BOOL onehot6) up to thousands (F32 slabs) — a strict loss every way.

via a **free-output** Equal→Pad (the `[1,10,30,30]` BOOL output is named `output` ⇒ scorer-skipped).
At cost 747 the charged tensors are: `onehot6 [1,10,3,6] BOOL` = **180** (the answer; irreducible),
`canvas_f [1,1,8,8] F32` = 196 (Conv output is F32; unavoidable as the gather source) + `canvas` u8 64,
projections/gathers ≤ ~160, INT64 index vectors ~104.

| tensor | bytes | irreducible? |

| `canvas_f` [1,1,8,8] F32 | 256 | YES — ORT Conv output dtype=input dtype=F32; crop needs all 8 rows (row=5 ⇒ rows 5,6,7). No integer-canvas path (ArgMax-collapse would be [1,1,30,30] I64=7200; Slice-of-input re-introduces the ×10). |

| locate scalars (rmax,cmax,rp,cp,r0,c0,r0f,c0f,ri,ci6) | ~80–100 | bbox-locate; can shave ~28–36 via I32 indices. |
| params (conv_w 40 + ids 10 + index/pad inits ~19) | 69 | conv_w 40 forced by the [1,10,2,2] collapse kernel; ids 10 = the 10 color comparators. |

Memory floor (irreducible 5 tensors) = 256+180+64+24+18 = **542**; + 69 params = **611 absolute** even with a

## Don't-do log

- **Crop must be N≥8, NOT 7.** The RANDOM generator caps `r0,c0` at 4 (gather index ≤ 6, so 7×7 looks
  safe on arc-gen-only oracles), BUT the bundled visible **TRAIN** set has a hand-authored `row=5`
  example → gather index 7 → a 7×7 crop **ERRORS** `Gather idx=7 out of bounds` on that pair (visible
  fails ⇒ certain hidden-0). N=8 covers index 7 (7<8) and is the minimum safe crop. (The old log's
  "N=10 minimum" was over-conservative; N=8 is provably safe and is the LIVE crop.)
  **Lesson: gate against the BUNDLED train/test, not just fresh arc-gen — hand-authored `validate()`
  examples can exceed the random generator's coordinate range.**
- The `[1,1,8,8]` F32 Conv canvas (196 B) is irreducible: ORT Conv output dtype = input dtype = F32;
  a u8 canvas needs that F32 precursor (consumed by the Cast). Don't try to "make the canvas u8 from
  the start" — it can't be done at the Conv.
- GatherND to fuse the row+col gather into one op is WORSE here: a `[3,6,2]` INT64 index plane (288 B,
  data-dependent ⇒ charged) exceeds the `rows3` [1,1,3,8] (24 B u8) it would save.

New pricing, no build warranted:
- **Joint locate is worse.** A single two-code Einsum still needs separate r/c values for the dynamic Slice, so the Less/Cast/ArgMin/Cast footprint is not meaningfully reduced. The one-Einsum vector form needs at least row/col selector bases (`[2,30]` plus `[2,30]`, or a larger 2-D weight) and adds >=60 params versus Aditya's shared `[30]` `pos_code`; scalar combined-code variants need larger threshold vectors plus Div/Mod to recover r/c.
- **Direct `GatherND` is worse.** The crop is a fixed contiguous 3x3 window, so #146 applies: dynamic Slice beats GatherND. Reading channel 0 directly would require a runtime INT64 index plane at least `[9,4]` = 288 B, before the 36 B gathered values and reshape/stack work, while Aditya's Slice path pays only `zstarts` 12 B + `zends` 12 B + `zero_crop` 36 B.
